session.question: In this fouling study, how did Actinobacteria relate ta the microbes on prepainted steel, and what other kinda microorganism was most dominant there?
session.answer:
Actinobacteria were among the dominant bacterial groups colonizing the prepainted steel surfaces, alongside Bacillus spp. and cyanobacteria. Thus, they were an important component of the bacterial fouling community on the steel. (huynh2016investigationofthe chunk 1)

The most dominant organisms overall, however, were fungi as shown by fluorescence in situ hybridization imaging. The fouled steel also included Cladosporium sp., Epicoccum nigrum, and Teratosphaeriaceae sp. (huynh2016investigationofthe chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-5ab9581f: The study found that Actinobacteria were among the dominant bacterial groups colonizing prepainted steel, along with Bacillus spp. and cyanobacteria. However, fluorescence in situ hybridization imaging showed that fungi were the most dominant organisms present on the fouled steel surfaces. The community also included Cladosporium sp., Epicoccum nigrum, and Teratosphaeriaceae sp., and overall diversity was low but varied by site and over time.
From Tran T. Huynh, Ili Jamil, Nicole A. Pianegonda, Stephen J. Blanksby, Philip J. Barker, Mike Manefield, and Scott A. Rice. Investigation of the microbial communities colonizing prepainted steel used for roofing and walling. MicrobiologyOpen, 2016. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/mbo3.425, doi:10.1002/mbo3.425.
